overview: 4-month, part-time (≈3 hrs/day) roadmap focused on intermediate backend web development with Django. Prioritizes core foundations (Python, OOP, data structures, algorithms, databases, version control), then moves to applied backend skills (Django, REST APIs, testing), infrastructure basics (Docker, CI/CD, AWS), and finishes with a capstone where you build, containerize, test, and deploy a real web service. Total available time ≈ 360 hours (4 months × ~30 days × 3 hrs/day). The plan compresses suggested depths to fit time while preserving dependencies and practical application.

topics: Python: syntax, variables, data types, control flow, functions, modules
Error handling and basic file I/O
OOP: classes/objects, simple inheritance, magic methods (dunder basics)
Git: init, add, commit, branch, merge; GitHub: repo, PR basics
Linux: shell commands, file permissions, SSH basics
Debugging: logging, print debugging, reading stack traces
objectives: Be productive writing and running Python code and simple modules
Understand and apply basic OOP patterns to structure code
Use Git and GitHub for version control and simple collaboration
Use the Linux shell to manage files and run services
Confidently reproduce and debug basic runtime errors
projects: Mini CLI utilities (e.g., todo list or CSV processor) stored in GitHub repositories
Setup dev environment: Python venv, VS Code/PyCharm, basic linting, and remote SSH access
resources: Automate the Boring Stuff / Real Python tutorials (Python fundamentals)
Official Python docs (errors, stdlib)
Pro Git book and GitHub Learning Lab (Git/GitHub)
LinuxCommand.org, Codecademy shell intro
VS Code or PyCharm debugger walkthroughs, short videos

topics: Python data structures: lists, tuples, sets, dicts and when to use them
Implement stacks, queues, simple trees and basic graph representations
Sorting and searching algorithms; recursion; Big-O analysis
Algorithm practice (LeetCode/Easy→Medium problems) with timed sessions
Unit testing basics: pytest/unittest, writing assertions, simple mocks
Code review: creating clear PRs and giving/receiving feedback
objectives: Implement and choose appropriate data structures for problems
Understand common algorithms and analyze their complexity
Solve medium-level algorithmic problems under practice conditions
Establish a habit of writing unit tests and using test runners
Participate in basic code reviews and improve code quality iteratively
projects: Collection of solved problems with well-documented solutions and tests (hosted on GitHub)
Small module that demonstrates data structures (e.g., in-memory task queue) with unit tests
resources: CS Dojo/Abdul Bari algorithm videos, Big-O cheat sheets
LeetCode (Easy/Medium) practice sets or HackerRank pledges
“Grokking Algorithms” (concise intro)
pytest documentation, official unittest docs
GitHub PR workflow guides and sample code review checklists

topics: Relational fundamentals: SELECT/INSERT/UPDATE/DELETE, JOINs, aggregates, CTEs
MySQL basics: setup, connectors (mysql-connector / PyMySQL), data types, simple admin tasks
Database design: ER diagrams, normalization, primary/foreign keys, indexing trade-offs
Django: project/app structure, models/migrations, ORM queries, views/URLs/templates, forms and authentication basics
Intro to HTTP methods & status codes; Postman: composing and testing requests
objectives: Design normalized schemas for small apps and write efficient SQL queries
Connect Django to a MySQL database and model domain entities with migrations
Build CRUD web pages in Django and understand request/response lifecycles
Design basic API endpoints and manually test them with Postman
projects: Build a simple Django CRUD application (e.g., blog or task manager) backed by MySQL with migrations and basic auth
Create a Postman collection that demonstrates CRUD operations and includes basic tests
resources: SQLBolt, Mode SQL tutorials, MySQL official docs
Django official tutorial and Django Girls tutorial
Django ORM cookbook, Real Python Django guides
Postman learning center, HTTP status code references

topics: DRF: serializers, viewsets, routers, basic permissions
JWT: token flow, integrating JWT with DRF, security considerations
Containerization: Dockerfile, images, containers, Docker Compose for local dev
CI/CD: GitHub Actions pipeline to run tests and build Docker images; simple deploy step
AWS fundamentals: EC2 and RDS overview, using AWS free tier to host a container or server; storing static/media (S3 concept)
Basic performance checks: identifying N+1 queries, simple caching ideas
objectives: Expose a RESTful API from your Django app with JWT-based authentication
Containerize the application and run multi-service local setup (app + db)
Create a basic CI pipeline to run tests and build artifacts
Deploy a simple containerized service to an AWS instance or minimal managed service
Deliver a working capstone with documentation, tests, and a deployable pipeline
projects: Capstone: Full-stack backend capstone — build a Django + DRF application (e.g., task manager with users), containerize it, add JWT auth, write tests, and deploy a basic instance on AWS. Include CI workflow and Postman collection.
Conduct a short code review cycle with a peer or mentor and iterate based on feedback
resources: Django REST Framework official docs and DRF tutorial
Simple JWT or djangorestframework-simplejwt docs
Docker docs, Dockerfile best practices, Docker Compose examples
GitHub Actions starter workflows and CI templates
AWS Getting Started tutorials (EC2, RDS, S3), DigitalOcean tutorials as lower-cost alternative
Articles on N+1 query detection and Django debugging/profiling

tips: Treat one day per week as a lighter review/reflection day: recap notes, fix a single bug, or write documentation.
Keep every project in GitHub and update the README as you progress — small, visible wins boost motivation.
Practice deliberate, short algorithm sessions (30–60 minutes) 3×/week instead of long marathons.
Automate small habits: start each coding session by running tests for 5 minutes to maintain test-first discipline.
When stuck, explain the problem aloud or in writing before searching — teaching is a powerful debugging tool.
Schedule weekly short demos (to a friend/peer/recording) to improve communication and solidify learning.
